title: Character Gameplay System
summary: Defines how element, profession, role, weapon, statistics, abilities, talents and relationships combine into a distinct playable identity.

headings.text: Do Not Break Multiple Fundamental Rules at the Same Time

blocks.text: Every playable character in Symphony of Justice should be built from several layers that define both who they are within the world and how they play in real time.
Character anatomy is organized around seven main components:
ELEMENT + PROFESSION + ROLE + WEAPON + STATISTICS + KIT + PERSONAL TALENT
These layers should not function as independent labels. Their combination should produce a coherent gameplay identity.
The goal is for the player to progressively understand:
“This character fights this way because their abilities represent who they are within Symphony of Justice.”
This direction follows the Game Vision, where characters are simultaneously strategic tools, connections to organizations, and different perspectives on the universe.
The Element defines part of a character’s supernatural capabilities and their relationship with the reaction system.
Historical documentation separates affinities into two main families:
Elemental magic: Water, Fire, Ice, Electro, Plant, Wind, and Earth.
Pure or special magic: Chaos, Illumination / Sanctification, Spectrum, and Seals.
Physical and Time Clock also exist as particular capabilities that do not necessarily participate in the same reactions.
However, the element does not determine the character’s role by itself.
Two Fire characters, for example, may function in completely different ways depending on their profession, personal talent, and kit.
Profession represents what the character knows how to do, or what they do within the world.
Examples include Doctor, Executioner, Chef, Vigilante, Prosecutor, Blacksmith, Summoner, Explorer, Guardian, Professor, Artist, and many others.
The documentation already proposes more than twenty professions and explicitly establishes that they may influence both exploration and gameplay.
It does not automatically determine the character’s combat role.
Role represents the character’s primary responsibility during an encounter.
What problem is this character expected to solve for the team?
A role may be oriented toward:
Historical documents already distinguish several archetypes such as Assassin, Explosive Fighter, Debuff Support, Helper Support, Stubborn Fighter, different Mage types, Tanks, and Marksmen.
In the current system, these are organized as main roles and specializations, described later in this document.
statistics and passives provided by equipment.
The documents already assign very different weapons even among similar professions, including swords, spears, bows, greatswords, scythes, and spellbooks.
The weapon helps define how a character feels to control, but it should not automatically define their function.
A sword user may be a healer, DPS, support, or hybrid depending on the kit.

The original documentation considers the following base statistics: HP, Attack, Defense, Energy Recharge, Critical Rate, Critical Damage, Unique Scaling, Alchemy, Elemental Resistance, and Elemental Damage.
To normalize the Character Gameplay System, they are organized as follows:
HP / Health: Determines how much damage the character can receive before becoming incapacitated.
ATK / Attack: Base statistic for abilities whose scaling depends on offensive power.
DEF / Defense: Reduces incoming damage or participates in defensive scaling.
Critical Rate: Probability of landing a critical hit.
Critical Damage: Additional multiplier applied by a critical hit.
Elemental Damage: Modifier associated with the character’s element.
Energy Recharge: Modifies the rate at which the character gains the resource required for their Ultimate.

Alchemy: A special statistic related to the effectiveness of elemental interactions and reactions. Historical documentation already presents it as a way to affect multipliers, weaknesses, and creations produced by reactions.
Elemental Resistance: Reduces damage received from specific elemental sources.
Each character may have a particular scaling statistic or rule.
The documentation explicitly establishes that scaling may vary according to the character’s kit and function.
Historical concepts such as Fortune, Taunt, Greed, Life Drain, or Attack Speed exist in earlier versions.

The underlying idea distinguishes statistics a character has by default from statistics obtained externally. Taunt may function in multiplayer or with summons by changing enemy targeting priority; Life Drain allows a character to heal through damage dealt; Attack Speed defines the time between strikes; and similar statistics may support specific gameplay goals. Their final status requires separate balance and systems review.
The Kit represents the complete set of actions and rules that determine how the character is controlled.
normal attacks + skills + Ultimate + passive + unique mechanic.
The intention is to prevent a new character from being merely a source of higher statistics. A new character should introduce a new form of interaction.
The Personal Talent represents what distinguishes a character even from other members of the same profession and element.
Historical documentation also refers to this concept as Personal Division or Unique Talent, indicating that it may alter synergies and change gameplay depending on team composition.
For example, Juro uses his own HP for certain abilities and progressively generates tentacles, making his relationship with missing HP an integral part of his gameplay.

The element determines what the character interacts with; the profession expresses what they know how to do, especially in cooperative Dungeon contexts; the role defines their responsibility; the weapon determines how they feel to control; and the personal talent determines why the character cannot simply be replaced by another.
The role system organizes characters according to the responsibility they fulfill during combat, not according to profession, element, or weapon.

Historical documentation contains numerous archetypes. To simplify design, balance, and communication to the player, these are consolidated into five main roles while preserving older concepts as specializations.
Its primary responsibility is dealing damage.
converting buffs and reactions into damage.

Historical documentation describes the Explosive Fighter as a character capable of dealing considerable damage while retaining shields, recovery, or damage reduction, while the Stubborn Fighter scales the longer they remain in combat.
normally does not surpass a pure DPS in burst damage or a Guardian in protection.
Its responsibility is protecting the team.
The documentation distinguishes between a Sentinel Tank, more focused on entering combat directly, and a Guardian Tank, specifically dedicated to protecting allies.
Its responsibility is increasing the team’s overall effectiveness.
Historical documentation differentiates between offensive debuff support and helper / healer support.
Its goal is not necessarily to deal damage directly.
Suki, for example, is already conceived as a Vigilante capable of applying and improving negative effects.
Characters may have a primary role and a secondary role.
However, a character should not excel at three or four responsibilities simultaneously without paying a significant cost.
The role defines what the character does for the team. The specialization defines how they do it.
Profession and role represent different concepts.
What responsibility does the character have in combat?
What does this person know how to do within the world, and how does that manifest in gameplay?
Historical documents explicitly establish this distinction. Professions affect exploration and gameplay and may facilitate certain functions, but they should not force a character into a single role.
Hizuka converts part of her healing into shielding, allowing her Doctor profession to participate directly in her gameplay identity.
Aligura already has a bonus related to elemental abilities performed by creatures.
Juro increases his potential as the enemy approaches death.
The document makes clear that a Chef could use the profession offensively through poisoning or defensively through healing.
This example summarizes the philosophy particularly well.
Each profession may provide up to three kinds of contribution:
Exploration Utility: An advantage associated with world activities.
Professional Synergy: An interaction with specific characters, systems, or elements.
Not every profession is required to provide all three.
Two Doctors should not necessarily function in the same way.
Doctor B: Poisons + healing over time.
All three still express Medicine, but their elements + roles + talents + weapons produce different results.

PROFESSION = shared language.
PERSONAL TALENT = individual interpretation.
Because current combat is real time, abilities must be designed around:
Each character uses the following structure as a reference:
It may contain approximately 3 to 6 hits depending on speed, weapon, and style.
Not every character needs exactly the same format.
A frequently used core ability with a short or medium cooldown.
It may provide mobility, support, control, or setup. It may also be conditional on Skill 1, functioning as a second cast, or transform while Skill 1 or the Ultimate is active.

A passive or central system that changes how the character plays and may even guide how the character should be built. For example: “Juro gains 0.05% Critical Damage for every 1,000 HP above X amount, up to a maximum of 25%.” This immediately communicates a possible build direction and intended use.

When applicable, it may function in both combat and exploration. Historical design gives particular weight to the second phase of Dungeons, where certain professions may enable interactions, missions, objectives, or access to additional sections of an area.
Long cooldown: abilities capable of significantly changing combat conditions.
Exact values belong to balance documentation.
A character may alter the standard structure.
holding an ability to charge or sustain it;
These exceptions should feel like identity, not an excuse to fill the interface with buttons.
Depth should come primarily from how abilities interact, not from having an excessive number of abilities.

Each character should possess a distinctive mechanic that can be explained briefly and recognized during gameplay. Historically, this design language has been associated with one of three “Gameplay Breaks.”
The three historically defined Gameplay Breaks are:
Mechanical Break: The character has a special mechanic that defines them or adapts them to their environment, allowing a distinct combat, sustain, or amplification capability.
Scaling Break: The character pushes scaling or percentage interactions to an unusually high level, creating exceptional statistical pressure that becomes difficult to contest if left unchecked.

Environment Break: The character becomes particularly effective because of encounter or team conditions. Examples include enemies being weak to a specific element, suffering additional disadvantages while shielded, or dealing HP damage that ignores shields. Characters designed to counter these circumstances gain situational value.
Juro is a clear precedent: he consumes HP, generates up to eight tentacles, and uses those tentacles throughout different parts of his kit.
“Juro converts his own survivability and the number of available tentacles into resources the player must manage.”
That represents the kind of identity the system seeks.
Several rules are proposed to avoid kits that are impossible to balance.
The mechanic may have several manifestations, but they should revolve around one main idea.
Do Not Break Multiple Fundamental Rules at the Same Time
uses HP instead of a normal resource;
they do not also need to ignore cooldowns, revive infinitely, and copy Ultimates. That exaggerated example illustrates the boundary.
One well-developed mechanical exception has more identity than five unrelated exceptions taped together.
Even an unusual character should continue using recognizable concepts:
The central mechanic must work without requiring duplicates.

The Legacy Card may expand possibilities, but it must not repair an incomplete kit. This follows the Game Vision principle that duplicates should not be the only way to make a character functional. The Legacy Card should enhance the kit through smaller improvements rather than make the kit work in the first place.
The central mechanic should be explainable in one or two sentences.

Some characters may intentionally be mechanically complex, with high execution demands and high rewards. Even in those cases, the basic idea of how they function should be explainable without requiring an excessive amount of time merely to understand what an ability does.
Relationships are one of the more distinctive features of Symphony of Justice.
Historical design already establishes that certain synergies may emerge not only from profession and element, but also from specific character pairings, in some cases modifying gameplay.
However, the system must avoid becoming:
“If you do not own X, Y is incomplete.”
These do not provide combat advantages.
They may represent friendship, rivalry, family, loyalty, love, conflict, or other relationships.
These do not require specific characters.
They work through categories such as:
Example: a character gains a bonus whenever an ally applies a shield.
The identity of that ally does not matter. This preserves composition freedom.
These are special interactions between specific characters.
They should not be the only way to make a kit functional.
An example is Dracken and Isabell. In the lore they are known as the Lovers, yet their combat styles and kits are intentionally opposite.
The central idea is that they complement each other through rotation structure, skill application, or the way their Ultimates can be used together.
Neither depends on the other being in the team, but pairing them can complement their kits without making either one incomplete alone.
Every character should function individually, improve through general systems, and gain additional flavor through specific relationships.
This prevents narrative and gameplay from becoming a mathematical prison.
This should become the official gameplay sheet for every character.
Element Type: Elemental / Pure / Special / Physical
[What should the player feel when controlling this character?]
Type: Damage / Support / Control / Mobility / Other
Same fields as Skill 1, when applicable.
Each upgrade should indicate whether it:
The original documentation conceives the Legacy Card as an important memory completed through fragments while simultaneously expanding the character’s kit.
This section does not replace the character’s complete narrative sheet. It only contains the information necessary to understand why their gameplay works in a particular way.
